kits.json.note: The audited bytes are recoverable and no kit has drifted materially, so this baseline is real. No kit has a per-record evidence section in any lane report, so it records integrity only, not screening.

rescue_cards.json.note: AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md records rescue-card SHA-256 4f8e47d0e93dcc95476f4e4bf8af0bcbfa866d6e5dca4fd63e54dd48fba2fc14 for the audited snapshot. Those bytes are in no object in this repository, reachable or unreachable, because the audit fingerprinted an uncommitted working tree. The audited baseline is therefore unrecoverable and is not reconstructed here: seeding it from current content would assert that today's text is what was screened. This baseline was established after the audit, catches drift from this point forward, and attests nothing about the audit.

amendments.rationale: Re-screened and accepted by the clinical owner. Post-audit change in 9425966 added topical tranexamic acid to equipment (500 mg/5 mL injectable solution on a pledget or soaking the pack, per local policy), the Zahed 2013 randomised trial supporting it, and matching search tags. No existing step, dose ceiling, contraindication or complication text was altered; the addition is an adjunct alongside the audited packing technique. The lane report's findings for this record stand.

Re-screened and accepted by the clinical owner. Post-audit change in fcd718f resolved a dose contradiction the audit did not catch: 30 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine is 150 mg, above the record's own weight-based ceiling. Volume is now capped by concentration in both equipment and steps, and the worked example shows the arithmetic. This tightens a stated maximum rather than widening one, so no audit finding is loosened by it.
